transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is... my head just feels really foggy lately. I work as a personal care aide, and I’ve been making these little mistakes in my client notes. I also keep forgetting what I was just about to do right in the middle of a shift. It’s just, you know, it really isn’t like me to be this scattered, so I wanted to come in and get it checked out.
How long have you been feeling this foggy sensation?
I'd say it's been about two weeks. This whole shift really started right after my uncle died... yeah, that was about two weeks ago.
Have you been feeling sad or down since your uncle passed away?

Yeah, I have. Lately, I just wake up with this... heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. I mean, I can still get through my shift and talk to my clients and everything, but inside, I just feel really sad and flat. It's just there all the time right now.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

Um, yeah, I think so. I haven't really noticed a change there. I mean, I still enjoy watching a game on the weekends or just relaxing on my days off. It's not like I've lost interest in my normal stuff... I just have that heavy feeling sitting in the background while I'm doing it.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything related to your uncle's death?

Yeah, I have. I just keep replaying what I should have done for my tío before he died. Like... I should have called him more often, or made the time to visit him sooner. I just end up feeling like I really failed him as family.
Have you noticed any change in your weight since your uncle passed away?
No, not really. My weight has stayed pretty much the same. I haven't noticed any changes or, you know, my clothes fitting differently or anything like that.
Have you had to take any days off work due to how you've been feeling?

I haven't actually taken any days off, no. But it is affecting things. Like at work, I've had to ask some of my coworkers to double-check my client documentation for me, just to make sure I didn't miss anything. And at home, my wife has had to take over paying some of the bills and handling the scheduling. I'm just... I'm not as reliable with the details right now.
Have you been avoiding social situations or gatherings since your uncle's death?

No, I haven't really been avoiding people. I mean, I still go to family things and see friends when they ask. I just... I might not be the life of the party right now, but I'm not hiding away or anything.
Have you been feeling like you're moving more slowly than usual?
No, I don't think so. Physically, I feel like I'm moving at my normal pace. I haven't felt weighed down or sluggish or anything like that.
Have you noticed yourself pulling back or participating less in hobbies or things you normally enjoy since your uncle passed away?

No, not really. I'm still doing the things I usually like to do. I haven't stopped any of my hobbies or anything like that. I still catch the games on the weekend and do my normal stuff, so I wouldn't say I've pulled back from any of that.
Have you felt less interested in things you usually enjoy doing since your uncle passed away?

No, I... I still enjoy them. Like I was just saying about my hobbies, I still like doing my normal stuff. I haven't really lost interest or stopped caring about the things I usually get a kick out of.
Have you felt like you're going through the motions when doing things you normally enjoy?
No, I wouldn't say that. When I'm doing my stuff, I'm actually into it. I'm not just... you know, doing it out of habit or faking it. I still genuinely get a kick out of it.
Have you felt like your interest in things has decreased significantly since your uncle passed away?
I feel like I'm repeating myself a bit here, doc, but no. My interest hasn't dropped off at all. Like I was saying, I still care about all the same stuff just as much as I did before he passed.
Have you noticed any days where you didn't feel like doing anything at all?
No, I haven't. Um... honestly, I haven't had any days like that. I get up, I go to work, I do my usual stuff. There hasn't been a time where I just sat around and didn't want to do anything at all.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but no longer find enjoyable since your uncle's death?

No, not really. I know you're asking it a few different ways, but it's still the same answer. There isn't anything I've just stopped enjoying. Everything I liked doing before he passed, I still like doing now. Nothing has really changed in that department.
Have you felt less enthusiastic about things you normally enjoy doing since your uncle passed away?

Look, doc, I... I feel like we're just going in circles now. No, I haven't felt less enthusiastic. Like I've been saying, my drive for the things I like is exactly the same. I know you have to be thorough, but it's really just a solid no to all these questions about losing interest or enjoyment.
Have you felt less excited or looking forward to things you normally enjoy since your uncle passed away?

Doc, I... I really don't know how else to say it. No. I still look forward to things just as much as I always have. My excitement hasn't dropped off at all. I know you're just doing your job, but the answer is really still no.
Are there any things you used to find pleasurable but now feel neutral about since your uncle passed away?

I... I really don't have a different answer for you. No. Nothing feels neutral. If I liked doing it before, I still like doing it now. I promise you, if there was something I had stopped caring about or lost interest in, I would just tell you, but there really isn't anything.
Do you feel like your reactions to your uncle's death are consistent with how you would expect yourself or others to feel in a similar situation?

Yeah, I... I think so. I mean, it's sad, obviously, because he was my uncle. But I feel like I'm handling it the way anyone else would. It just feels like a normal reaction to losing a family member, you know? I'm grieving, but I'm not falling apart or anything.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of feeling sad, empty, and guilty, as well as their preoccupation with their uncle's death and what they could have done differently, are consistent with a diagnosis of acute grief reaction, also known as bereavement. However, given the context and the specific symptoms described, the most accurate diagnosis is adjustment disorder, which is characterized by the development of emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable stressor, in this case, the death of the patient's uncle.
